answer: In an agent marketplace for dune surveys, basalt samples, and jade appraisals, each seller identity must lock 100 credits as a bond before accepting work. A contract slashes that bond if the seller misses a delivery deadline recorded on the shared ledger. Creating names is free, but activating 1,000 fake sellers ties up 100,000 credits, and coordinated non-delivery burns their bonds. Splitting into identities therefore does not multiply unbacked selling capacity.
